entries.label: Display Name
entries.help: The name other people see on your messages.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Email
entries.help: The address you sign in with. Changing it asks for your password.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A local account only. An account from a sign-in provider shows it read only.

entries.label: Role
entries.help: Your platform role. An administrator changes it under Admin, Users.
entries.who: Nobody changes it. The page only shows it.

entries.label: Change Password
entries.help: Sets a new password after you confirm the current one.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A local account only.

entries.label: Add a passkey
entries.help: Adds a passkey to sign in with, after you confirm your password.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A local account only, and only when OtoDock is open at its secure address.

entries.label: Passkey
entries.help: Renames or removes one of your passkeys. Each change asks for your password.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Use an authenticator app
entries.help: Adds time-based codes as a second factor, with recovery codes to keep. Remove takes it off again.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A local account only.

entries.label: Theme
entries.help: Choose how the dashboard looks. Kept in this browser.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Chat activity
entries.help: Compact folds tool activity into expandable summaries. Kept in this browser.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Subscription usage alerts
entries.help: This watches your connected Claude and ChatGPT accounts. You get a notification when one passes 90% of its weekly limit. You get another when it reaches the limit.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Agents know which app I am looking at
entries.help: While an app is on your screen, the agent you talk to learns its name. Nobody else learns what you are looking at.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Agents may open apps on my screen
entries.help: An agent can bring up one of its apps for you. In the chat you are in, it opens right away. Anywhere else, you get a notice with an Open button.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Wake word
entries.help: To start a voice conversation, say “Hey OtoDock” on any dashboard page. You can also say “Hey” plus an agent’s name. Detection runs only on this device. Audio never leaves it until a conversation starts.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: The microphone is only on while the dashboard is open.

entries.label: Record diagnostics
entries.help: Records what the wake word hears on this device, for troubleshooting.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: Under Troubleshooting, shown while the wake word is on.

entries.label: Clear my memory across all agents
entries.help: Deletes the personal memories agents captured about you, across every agent. It asks you to type a confirmation first.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Add an account
entries.help: Signs you in to a service your agents use on your behalf, or saves its credentials. A service that takes one account offers no second.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A service is listed when a tool of one of your agents uses it.

entries.label: Connected account
entries.help: One account of a service: its label, the services it reaches, the default star, and Reconnect, Disconnect or Remove. Agents not bound to another account use the default.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A personal access token takes an optional account label. An account whose sign-in can no longer be renewed shows Reconnect needed with the reason.
entries.item: a connected account of a service

entries.group: Use this account for specific agents
entries.label: Use this account for specific agents
entries.help: Binds one of your agents to this account. On GitHub you can limit the repositories the agent reaches in your chats, or make it read only.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Install on GitHub
entries.help: Picks the repositories on GitHub this account reaches. Until the app is installed somewhere, the account reaches nothing.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A GitHub account connected through a GitHub App.

entries.label: + Subscribe to events
entries.help: Subscribes to a service's events, for yourself or for an agent this account serves. A personal subscription fires your own triggers and apps.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: A service with an event API. Subscribing as an agent needs the manager role on it, and a Personal-only agent is not offered.

entries.label: Subscription
entries.help: One event subscription: its address and secret to copy, and Delete.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: + Create key
entries.help: Makes a personal API key for your webhook triggers. The key shows once.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
names: triggers: fire your own webhook triggers

entries.label: API key
entries.help: One of your personal API keys, with when it was made and last used. Revoke ends it at once.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Pair Machine
entries.help: Connects your own computer, so agents can run on it. The pair command runs once on that machine.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: Hidden when the build lacks the feature. A notice replaces the page when an administrator turned user pairing off.

entries.label: Remove machine
entries.help: Unpairs the machine. A machine an administrator paired for the platform is removed under Admin, Remote Machines.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Allow full FS
entries.help: On, agents can read and write any path your OS user can reach. Off, they stay in their agent folders and your home folder. The home folder limit is a guardrail, not full isolation.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Computer control
entries.help: Grants agents the mouse, keyboard and screen, a browser on this computer, or the applications on it. Turn one on only on a computer you trust them with.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Browser mode
entries.help: A dedicated profile, or your own browser through the Playwright Extension and its token. Browser profile names the profile that has the extension. With a saved token you can also let unattended runs use it.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
names: Also let unattended runs like scheduled tasks, triggers, calls and meetings use this browser. Off, they cannot use it at all.
entries.note: Shown once browser control is granted.

entries.group: Run these agents on this machine
entries.label: Run these agents on this machine
entries.help: Ticks the agents whose chats run on this machine for you. An agent already on another machine says so.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Connect your Claude account
entries.help: Signs in to your Claude or ChatGPT subscription, so your own chats and agents run on it. The Claude popup uses the browser's session at platform.claude.com.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Use an API key instead
entries.help: Saves an API key of the engine's vendor in place of a subscription.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Subscription
entries.help: One connected account, with its status and usage windows. Reconnect revives an expired login or renews one that ends soon. Remove takes it off.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.item: a connected account or API key

entries.label: Personal use
entries.help: Use this account for your own chats.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Shared with agents
entries.help: Add this account to the shared subscriptions your agents use.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.note: Platform administrators only.

entries.label: Voice playback
entries.help: What reads replies aloud: this device, the platform's speech service, or Auto.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: Shown when the administrator's policy is User's choice. Otherwise the platform policy sets it.

entries.label: Dictation
entries.help: What listens when you dictate: this device, the platform's speech service, or Auto.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: Shown when the administrator's policy is User's choice. Also in Safari, and on an iPhone or iPad, under Native preferred with a speech provider.

entries.label: Dictation language
entries.help: The language the mic recognizes. Set it to dictate in a language other than English. Automatic starts in your browser language. Within a second or two, it moves to the language you speak. Without a speech service, or with Dictation set to Native, this device listens in its own language.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: Hidden when chat audio is off. The chat's microphone button also picks it.

entries.label: Voice
entries.help: Preferred device voice for native playback on this device. Set one language at a time. Kept in this browser.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.
entries.note: Shown when this device has voices.

entries.label: Usage
entries.help: Your platform API use this month and this week, with your own accounts beside it. A daily chart and a per-agent list follow.
entries.who: Nobody changes it. The page only shows it.

entries.label: Week %
entries.help: Caps your own connected accounts on each engine. Cap them at a share of their weekly window, or at the matching API cost. The first cap reached stops your new chats, or moves them onto an API key. Empty means no cap.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Set cap
entries.help: Caps what your own Anthropic or OpenAI API keys spend, by month and by week.
entries.who: Any signed-in person, on their own account.

entries.label: Company Name
entries.help: Shown as a heading in every agent's instructions.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: General Instructions
entries.help: Rules and context every agent reads with its own instructions.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Platform subscriptions and API keys
entries.help: The subscriptions, API keys, local model servers and model lists the whole platform runs on. Each model has a tier and a price.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: This install
entries.help: The running version, whether a newer release is out, and the license and billing. A license key is pasted and saved here.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.item: the license, the version and the billing

entries.label: Chat audio policy
entries.help: The chat audio policy: Native only, Native preferred, Platform only or User's choice. Also the speech providers with their keys, voices and defaults.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Phone servers and routes
entries.help: The phone servers and the routes, each with its agent, language, transfer targets and PIN. Also the call log, the caller data and the languages automatic detection may pick.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Require Two-Factor Authentication
entries.help: Every password account must add a passkey or an authenticator app before it signs in again.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.note: Refused while it would lock the administrator out.

entries.label: Sharing
entries.help: Whether people may share apps and chats with agents, with departments and by link. Also whether a link may go without a password, and the longest a share lasts.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Platform Timezone
entries.help: Used for scheduled tasks and for the date and time agents see in messages.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Login Session Duration
entries.help: Hours of inactivity before a user must sign in again.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.note: Active users stay signed in, so it only signs out idle sessions.

entries.label: Allow users to pair their own remote machines
entries.help: Users can pair their own machines, like laptops or home servers. Their agents can then run there.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.note: Turning it off disconnects every user-paired machine at once and blocks new pairings.

value.confirm: Off disconnects every user-paired machine at once, removes the machine choices people made and refuses new pairings. On lets people pair their own machines again.

entries.label: Fall back to local when a user's machine is offline
entries.help: If a user's chosen machine is offline, the session runs on the platform instead.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: On, a chat whose machine is offline runs on the platform instead. Off, it waits for the machine.

entries.label: Fall back to local when the agent's remote target is offline
entries.help: When a machine an admin chose is offline, the session runs on the platform instead.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.note: Off by default, because an admin often picks a machine to keep the data there.

value.confirm: On, an agent whose machine is offline runs on the platform, so its data may leave the machine. Off, it waits for the machine.

entries.label: Interactive terminal sessions
entries.help: Chats and tasks can run Claude Code or Codex as a live dashboard terminal. Off, every session runs the standard way and the interactive switches are hidden.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: Off hides the terminal switches everywhere and every new session runs the standard way. On brings the terminals back.

entries.label: Read subscription usage from the provider
entries.help: OtoDock asks Claude and ChatGPT for each connected account's session and weekly usage and prefers the account that resets first. Off, the shared subscriptions balance by recorded cost only.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: Off stops reading the usage windows from Claude and ChatGPT, and the AI Engines cards lose their usage bars. On reads them again.

entries.label: Clean up old chat session files
entries.help: Chats left untouched for the set period lose their session files, here and on the machines they ran on. Their full history stays saved.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: On, chats left untouched for the set period lose their session files, here and on the machines they ran on. Their history stays. Off keeps every file.

entries.label: Archive of removed people
entries.help: A removed person's folders are kept in an archive for the set number of days, then deleted.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: On, a removed person's archived folders are deleted after the set number of days. Off keeps every archive for ever.

entries.label: Automatic MCP Updates
entries.help: Once a week, in a quiet window, OtoDock applies available updates to community MCPs. Only failures notify admins.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: On, community MCPs update once a week on their own. Off, every update waits for an admin.

entries.label: Ask for a store rating
entries.help: The Android and iOS apps ask each person to rate OtoDock in Google Play or the App Store. They ask twice at most, after something went well.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: On, the Android and iOS apps ask each person for a store rating twice at most. Off, they never ask.

entries.label: Days before the second ask
entries.help: The second store rating ask comes at least this many days after the first. From 30 to 730.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

value.confirm: The second ask comes at least this many days after the first.

entries.label: Add User
entries.help: Adds a person with an invite link or a temporary password.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: User
entries.help: A person's platform role and their role on each agent. Also whether they may use the platform's API credentials, a password reset and deletion.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Usage and Limits
entries.help: The platform's totals and costs, each person's usage with a limit, agent budgets and the role defaults.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: MCP server
entries.help: Every installed tool with its switch, settings, instances and updates. Install takes a ZIP, Browse Community the catalog.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Skill package
entries.help: Every installed skill package with its updates and the catalog to browse.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Request
entries.help: An agent's request for a tool or a skill, approved with an instance when the tool takes one.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Pair New Machine
entries.help: Pairs a machine for the whole platform, where agents run by default.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Machine
entries.help: A machine's capabilities, versions, capacity, updates and grants. The people's own machines are listed too, each removable.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Every role of its agents runs here
entries.help: Off, the chats of editors, contributors and viewers run on the OtoDock platform, as the machine has no sandbox. On, they run on the machine with its access. An outside caller always runs on the platform.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
entries.note: Only the agents whose default place is this machine. Turning it on asks first.

entries.label: Share
entries.help: Every share to people, agents and departments and every link on the install, each revocable.
entries.who: A platform administrator.

entries.label: Report
entries.help: The agent replies people flagged, newest first, with who reported and why. Mark one handled or dismiss it, restore it from the closed list, or delete it.
entries.who: A platform administrator.
